items.excerpt: A survey by AI detector Originality.ai of 2,034 paperback religion books for sale on Amazon found that the majority were likely written by AI, including around three-quarters of titles on Hinduism, Taoism, and witchcraft. The findings put hard numbers on how far AI-generated 'slop' has penetrated a mainstream Amazon category.

A freelance book editor describes what changed in her craft and her contracts after editing two generative-AI-assisted manuscripts. Inexperienced authors may believe AI use improves their manuscript, but there's a cost that now shows up as extra fees and a rewritten client agreement.

Machine readers replacing human readers can sound like a threat. This post argues publishers are already well prepared to structure, tag and package content for AI consumption — reframing metadata and format work as the new front line of discovery.

The central risk of AI in publishing is not hallucination but 'cognitive debt': the gradual erosion of the human capacities that give scholarship its originality, integrity, and meaning. Part 2 lays out what an adaptive publisher's workflow should look like.

How Ukraine's academic publishing sector is confronting a global monograph crisis with unexpected urgency and innovation, using AI-era open-access tooling to move from charity recipient to intellectual partner.

A Villanova University study finds readers struggle to distinguish AI-generated stories from human work — and often rate the AI stories more highly. ALLi unpacks what that means for indie authors competing on craft.

Spotify is rolling out AI-powered audiobook playlists, a voice chatbot, and one-click series continuation, as Premium subscribers surpass 300M. ALLi looks at what the new discovery surface means for indie audiobook publishers.

Dan Holloway reports on the Indie Manga Alliance launch, Libro.fm's move into e-books, and the study showing readers who can't spot AI stories — a roundup of the week's structural shifts for independent creators.

If LLMs can continually update their content by ingesting new editions of textbooks as they come out, instructors and schools may drop textbook adoptions altogether in favor of AI 'substitutes,' the new U.S. textbook-author suit against OpenAI argues.

As AI licensing, microdeals, and expansion into new territories and formats proliferate, publishers need new reporting and rights-tracking practice to maintain trust with the creators whose work is being licensed.

Google Play Books' AI-powered Book Insights has launched for thousands of select English titles, adding in-book recaps and explanations to the reading surface. Google did not say if or when the tool will expand to non-English books.

A full rundown of the AI-driven audiobook features Spotify has shipped in recent months — prompted playlists, natural-language book Q&A, series tracking and Page Match — and what each changes for listeners and publishers.
Readers gave higher ratings to AI-written stories in a new study, AI is showing up in fanfiction communities, and library workers face a fresh set of AI-era collection questions.

Anthropic introduces watermarks, journalists test AI-detection tools against real manuscripts, and Claude generates a novel about writing a novel with Claude — a survey of where detection actually stands for editors.

At its Anime NYC 2026 panel, HarperCollins' new KAZÉ US manga imprint laid out its launch slate and stated flatly that it will not use AI translations — naming its human editorial, art-direction and design team instead.
